kept.heading: CHECK YOUR AI VISIBILITY
60-70% OF INFLUENCER BRIEFS NOW FAVOR MID-TIER CREATORS AS BRANDS QUESTION COST OF MEGA INFLUENCERS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands are favoring mid-tier creators as engagement and measurable performance matter more than follower count. Creators with 50K–500K followers can deliver lower CPVs, while historical views, watch time, and audience fit increasingly shape pricing decisions. Mega creators still command premiums when they offer mass reach or cultural relevance, but brands are pushing for fees that better reflect expected campaign performance.

kept.heading: WHY I AM BULLISH ON CHATGPT ADS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI can build an effective ad model if it keeps ads separate from answers and clearly labels them, similar to early Google AdWords. ChatGPT Ads reached $1B in annualized revenue in under 200 days, suggesting strong advertiser demand before the format has fully matured. Running shoes, travel, and price comparisons are especially promising because users now ask ChatGPT to research these commercial decisions instead of using Google.

kept.heading: 10 UNCONVENTIONAL WAYS TO BRAG ABOUT YOUR CUSTOMERS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Customer proof lands harder as a story or a stunt than as a logo row. Deel lists Snoop Dogg as a customer, Hinge commissioned novels from real couples' stories, and Shopify lit up the Las Vegas Sphere with every merchant's first sale. Smaller versions work too, like turning a "too advanced" one-star review into an ad or showing "customer since" dates under logos.

kept.heading: GREAT PRODUCTS NEED GREAT STORIES (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Great products still need strong stories that help people imagine how they fit into everyday life. Lead with the customer experience rather than technical capabilities, and show the human outcome the product enables. VisiCalc gave people a clear reason to buy the Apple II, while Tesla could frame FSD around making long-distance travel less exhausting rather than simply highlighting autonomous driving. Turn complex technology into a relatable vision of what life could look like.

kept.heading: SET UP YOUR CHATGPT ADS FOR SUCCESS: FIVE BEST PRACTICES FOR CREATING CAMPAIGNS DESIGNED TO PERFORM (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Join the ChatGPT Ads team to explore 5 best practices for creating campaigns. Through guidance and live demos, they'll show how these practices come to life in Ads Manager. The free webinar will take place on September 24 at 9:30 AM PT.

kept.heading: AI CITATION OUTREACH: A SEMRUSH & CLAUDE WORKFLOW (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This guide provides a step-by-step workflow for using Semrush and Claude Code to find and prioritize third-party pages that influence AI citations and brand visibility. It shows how to export citation data, configure Claude to analyze hundreds of pages for gaps or inaccuracies, validate its recommendations, and turn the findings into targeted outreach. It also covers tracking publisher responses and changes in AI citations over time to measure whether the outreach improves brand visibility.

kept.heading: 5 SPICY AI MARKETING TAKES (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI is changing marketing without necessarily reducing demand for marketers. Leaner teams may be offset by the growing number of businesses needing distribution. Chat ads could become a major ad format as LLM usage grows. Shared repositories can preserve institutional knowledge and give AI better context. Employee-generated content can extend brand reach through trusted voices. As AI handles more digital interactions, IRL events may become more valuable for creating human connection and closing deals.

kept.heading: CHATGPT NOW KNOWS WHAT YOU DO ON OTHER WEBSITES VIA AD COLLECTOR (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI's ad pixel uses a one-year __obi cookie tied to ChatGPT accounts and sends data to OpenAI when an advertiser's tag loads. It also collects hashed emails and phone numbers, unencrypted city and postal codes, and page paths containing medical and debt topics. The pixel works for logged-out users but appears limited to Chrome on Android, as iOS browsers block it.

kept.heading: ‘NOT ENOUGH USAGE': YOUR BIGGEST CHURN REASON IS A BROKEN HABIT LOOP (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Usage churn drives 26-40% of subscription app cancellations, often because users fail to build a lasting habit rather than because of price. Instead of defaulting to discounts, analyze engagement before cancellation to find where the habit loop breaks. Weak triggers may call for timely re-engagement, while poor onboarding or unclear value requires helping users reach meaningful outcomes sooner. Retention improves when the fix addresses why usage dropped rather than treating “not enough usage” as the root cause.

kept.heading: MANAGING THE AI MANDATE UPWARD (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Growth marketers have an edge over executives through their proximity to the work and understanding of LLMs.

kept.heading: MARKETERS TWICE AS LIKELY TO TRUST HUMAN REPORTS OVER AI, DESPITE HIGHER ERROR RATES (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Only 35% of marketers trust AI-generated reports without checks, versus 64% for human reports.

kept.heading: IT'S TIME TO RETHINK REDDIT'S ROLE IN THE MEDIA PLAN (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit can now play a broader role in media plans because its users already show strong purchase intent across categories, not just gaming or IT. New bidding options, lead generation, and age targeting give advertisers more control, and early tests of the new bidding structures showed a 15% reduction in CPA. Brands can treat Reddit as a performance channel when they have a strong measurement framework, rather than limiting it to experimental or upper funnel spend. Reddit still needs to preserve the authenticity that creates its value, since making ads too intrusive could undermine the user behavior that generates purchase intent in the first place.

kept.heading: GOOGLE'S OWN NOTEBOOKLM BECOMES A TARGET FOR PARASITE SEO (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A public Google NotebookLM report was cited as an AI Overview source within 24 hours of being published. Public notebooks promoting e-bike and peptide coupon codes, crypto refunds, backlink tools, and Instagram-engagement services are now showing up indexed on Google's own domain, borrowing ranking trust that a standalone site wouldn't have. Blocking crawler access and adding noindex work differently, too, and applying either broadly would also remove the legitimate study guides and business manuals the feature was built for.

kept.heading: YOUR CONTENT ISN'T BAD, BUT NOBODY KNOWS WHY THEY SHOULD CARE (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The clearest diagnostic is whether someone could describe what a brand talks about in one sentence when recommending them to a friend, and a vague answer usually means the positioning, not the writing, is the problem. People don't follow accounts they vaguely find interesting - they follow accounts that feel predictable in a good way, recognizable rather than random. A content pillar, a specific territory like social strategy or industry trends rather than an occasional topic, gives someone a consistent answer to that test instead of a different subject every day.

kept.heading: THE NEW RULES OF PODCAST ADVERTISING (32 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Podcast advertising is evolving as video and creator-led formats reshape how brands reach listeners. This guide looks at how video affects podcast performance, why audiences skip fewer ads than expected, and why smaller shows can outperform larger ones.

kept.heading: BLOGGING STATISTICS 2026 (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reported blog performance just hit an all-time low, with only 13.9% of respondents calling results strong, and the cause traces back to abandoned tactics rather than AI. Influencer collaboration, the single strongest predictor of success in the dataset at 2.6x the benchmark, has dropped from 25% of respondents in 2017 to 7% today, while original research, keyword research, and formal human editing have all declined too. AI use jumped from near zero to 92% in three years, yet users and non-users report strong results at the same rate, with only non-users skewing toward disappointing ones.

kept.heading: HOW TO USE AI TO BE MORE CREATIVE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Refining an idea with AI made it rated 30% more creative than not using AI at all, though the type of AI feedback needs to match the idea's maturity. Mature ideas refined through AI-written text came out 18% more creative than the same ideas refined through AI-generated images. Vague ideas benefited more from AI images instead. Images make an idea feel finished and discourage further refinement, while text leaves gaps that force more imaginative thinking.

kept.heading: THE BEST BRANDS MAKE THEMSELVES AT HOME (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands are optimising for visibility when they should be building memory. As AI makes it easier to produce more content, physical brand objects can create lasting connections that digital ads often lack. The strongest objects are distinctive enough to identify without a logo, useful or emotionally meaningful enough to keep, and rooted in something the brand genuinely owns. Starting with what a brand can make rather than what content a channel needs can lead to fewer, more memorable ideas that generate organic digital content.

kept.heading: THE TRUTH ABOUT BRAIN ROT: IT'S A CRY FOR HELP (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: “Brain rot” may look like evidence of declining attention spans, but Gen Z participants describe it as a response to an attention economy that constantly demands engagement. Absurd, meaningless content can feel like a break from polished, monetized media, even as endless scrolling leaves people drained and guilty. The deeper problem is the social media infrastructure that optimizes for attention rather than users' well-being.

kept.heading: APPLOVIN GROWS 60% Y/Y ROUNDING TO $20BN IN ANNUAL PLATFORM AD SPEND (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Over a billion people play mobile games daily, and relevant in-game ads are treated as a discovery mechanism for products that those players were not already seeking.

kept.blurb: TLDR MARKETING 2026-09-24

kept.heading: ADVERTISING IS GOING AI. TV ISN'T (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: By 2030, 27% of ad revenue could flow through AI-powered platforms. TV is moving slower. North American TV ad revenue is expected to grow just 3% in 2026, excluding political spending. Complex buying workflows and fragmented inventory make automation harder. AI could simplify TV buying, but it needs strong first-party data to work well.

kept.heading: MORE LOWER-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS FEEL FINANCIALLY VULNERABLE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Financially vulnerable US households rose from 15% to 17% in 2026, while fewer than 70% said they paid all bills on time over the past year. Low-income consumers have shifted more than $10 billion from discretionary purchases toward essentials since 2019, as prices for that group have risen 35% since January 2018. Consumer spending has still held steady in 2026, but many consumers are tapping into their savings to keep spending. This may not be sustainable if inflation, gas prices, and other costs continue to rise.

kept.heading: CALIFORNIA WILL FINE CREATORS $5,000 A POST FOR HIDDEN POLITICAL ADS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: California now allows fines of up to $5,000 per post for creators who fail to disclose paid political content from campaigns. AB 1130 gives the Fair Political Practices Commission enforcement powers that were previously missing. The law applies when creators are paid by campaign committees to support or oppose candidates or ballot measures. It doesn't cover unpaid political opinions. The law follows growing use of influencers in political campaigns and similar disclosure efforts elsewhere.

kept.heading: THE PERFECTLY OPTIMIZED PAGE FOR AEO (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A visual checklist showing the 6 key elements of a page optimized for AEO. Allowing major AI crawlers and server-side rendering makes the page accessible, while four to six direct sentences near the top give AI a concise answer to extract. Tables, lists, clear heading hierarchies, and FAQs make information easier to parse, and pages less than three months old are reportedly 3x more likely to earn citations.

kept.heading: I BUILT A GROWTH TEAM OF AGENTS TO RUN A 6 FIGURES BUSINESS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: An agent growth team can take over drafting and routing but should never take over sending. One solo operator pairs an orchestrator with about ten channel agents, covering everything from SEO to paid media to lifecycle email, each tied to a share of a 900-signup, 200-customer monthly target. Every task goes on a Todoist board that separates decisions from execution, and each card must say what the task is, why it matters, and where to click. Finished cards trigger the next agent's follow-up automatically, so the founder only approves and sends.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING GPT-6 SOL AND LUNA (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, two faster and more affordable models for everyday work, coding, computer use, and AI agents. Both bring improvements from GPT-6 Astra, including stronger factuality and collaboration. GPT-6 Sol costs $2 input and $10 output per 1M tokens, while Luna costs $0.10 input and $0.50 output, both 50% cheaper than GPT-5.6 promotional pricing.

kept.heading: AI POLLING: HOW SYNTHETIC SURVEYS COULD PREDICT REAL BEHAVIOR (20 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: People answer surveys as the person they want to be rather than the one they are, and synthetic surveys try to close that gap by simulating behavior instead of asking. AI personas built from interviews and behavioral records can return results in hours at about half the cost of human panels, and incumbents like Gallup and Qualtrics are already testing them. The simulations tend to match overall results but miss on subgroups and on questions outside their training data, where they rarely admit uncertainty.

kept.heading: WHAT WOULD A CHILD-FREE INTERNET LOOK LIKE? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Australia's under-16 social media ban deactivated 4.7M accounts, yet more than 80% of surveyed children still used age-restricted services. A “child-free” internet could push young users toward gaming, messaging, and smaller platforms, making their activity harder to monitor. Children could also remain visible through adult-run family influencer accounts. The shift could make young consumers' influence less visible to brands while limiting children's access to online communities and digital experiences.

kept.heading: AI AGENT CALLS THAT ARE ACTUALLY MADE BY HUMANS IN A CALL CENTER (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta pitched the feature publicly as AI, but internal posts describe a "human agent layer," and at least one tester only found out after the call that a person had placed it.

kept.heading: ONLY 11% OF SMALL MERCHANTS ARE READY FOR AI SHOPPING AGENTS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The bottleneck is merchant infrastructure rather than AI reasoning.
